### ESLint Repair Commit (`eb671ab` vs `94c4d199`)

Three mechanical changes only. I verified each is semantically inert:

**1. `preserveDeclinedConsent` extracted (`analytics.ts:127–131`).**
Identical code, lifted from inside the `recorded === 'false'` branch to a named module-scope function. No behavioral difference.

**2. `refreshAnalyticsConsent` extracted (`analytics.ts:365–368`).**
Arrow function `refresh` that was local to `attachConsentListeners` becomes a named module-scope function passed directly to `addEventListener`. Listeners fire identically; the function body is unchanged.

**3. Branch reordering in `migrateAnalyticsConsent` (`analytics.ts:154–167`).**
The prior code used `else if (recorded !== null)` (catch-all invalid state) followed by `else` (fresh install, `recorded === null`). Post-repair: `else if (recorded === null)` names the null case, `else` is the true catch-all. At the point this ladder is reached, `recorded` can only be `null` or some unexpected non-`'true'`/non-`'false'` string — the two branches are exhaustive and their swap preserves exact semantics. I traced all paths: `recorded === 'true' && explicit` returns early; `legacy` captures both implied-true and null-with-old-data; `recorded === 'false'` is next; the reordered pair handles the remainder identically.

**No privacy behavior changed by this repair.**

### Full Privacy Correctness Review

**Consent gate (`analytics.ts:43–52`).**
`hasAnalyticsConsent()` requires three independent conditions: `CONSENT_KEY === 'true'`, `CONSENT_VERSION_KEY === '2'`, and `source === null || source === 'user'`. `consentBlocked = true` short-circuits immediately. Storage exceptions set `consentBlocked`, call `stopAnalytics()`, and return false. Fail-closed.

**Migration never implies consent (`analytics.ts:132–170`).**
`recorded === 'true' && explicit` is the only path that preserves consent, and it requires both the version key and a user or null source. All legacy-true installs reach the `legacy = true` branch, which sets `consentBlocked = true`, writes `reason = 'legacy-reset'`, purges identity and queue via `clearAnalyticsData()` inside `stopAnalytics()`. Tested in four cases: pre-banner install with identity only, with implied true, with queue, and all three together.

**`setAnalyticsConsent` revocation (`analytics.ts:78–99`).**
`consentBlocked = true` fires before anything else, so any re-entrant call during the write sequence returns false. `stopAnalytics()` increments `consentGeneration` and aborts all `activeRequests`. When `allow = false`: CONSENT_KEY/VERSION/SOURCE removed first, then CONSENT_KEY='false' written. The test at line 103 of `analytics-consent.test.mts` verifies offline queue cleared; line 109 verifies identity cleared.

**Generation guard prevents stale init completing (`analytics.ts:373–435`).**
`const generation = consentGeneration` captured at init entry; `const allowed = () => generation === consentGeneration && isAnalyticsAllowed()` checked at every async boundary. Revocation increments `consentGeneration`, breaking the captured closure. The test "late failed response after revocation cannot retry" (`analytics-sdk-lifecycle.test.mjs:135`) verifies that held requests are aborted and sends.length stays at 2 after opt-out. The test "revocation while web initialization waits" verifies Vercel is never injected.

**Transport: no SDK, no retry (`analytics.ts:397–425`).**
Direct `fetch` POST to `/i/v0/e/` (web) or `$POSTHOG_HOST/i/v0/e/` (desktop). Each request gets its own `AbortController` stored in `activeRequests`. `stopAnalytics()` calls `controller.abort()` for every active request. Timeout is 10 s, cleared in `.finally()`. `credentials: 'omit'`, `keepalive: false`. The "stalled capture is aborted at the bounded timeout" test (`analytics-sdk-lifecycle.test.mjs:241`) mocks timers and confirms the signal aborts at exactly 10 000 ms with no second send.

**Vercel independently gated (`analytics.ts:387–393`).**
`inject({ beforeSend: event => isAnalyticsAllowed() ? event : null })` called only once, inside the `!vercelInitialized` guard. `beforeSend` re-checks at send time, so revocation mid-session takes effect without a reload. Test "web analytics needs consent independently of the PostHog key" (`analytics-sdk-lifecycle.test.mjs:208`) verifies `vercel.length === 0` before consent, `=== 1` after, and `beforeSend` returns null after revocation.

**Offline queue guarded at enqueue (`analytics.ts:444`).**
`if (!isAnalyticsAllowed()) return;` added to `enqueueOffline`. The pre-existing guard in `flushOfflineQueue` loop (`if (!isAnalyticsAllowed() || !captureInstance) return;`) is intact.

**`safeSetItem` return value.**
Returns `true` on success, `false` on any failure (quota or SecurityError), never throws. The `versionWritten` compound in `setAnalyticsConsent` requires all four writes to succeed before `consentBlocked` is cleared. If any fails, `consentBlocked = !false = true`, keeping the session opted out. Verified in the "storage failures block initial capture" lifecycle test.

**Reset notice nonmodal (`AnalyticsConsentBanner.ts:32–50`).**
`role="status"`, `aria-live="polite"`, no `aria-modal`. Only one button (Dismiss), whose click handler calls `notice.remove()`. No path to enable analytics from the notice. `markAnalyticsResetNoticeSeen()` is called on mount (not on dismiss), so the session flag is set regardless of whether the user interacts. The banner test (`analytics-reset-notice.test.mts:17`) checks `aria-modal` absent, focus unchanged, `buttons.length === 1`, and `hasAnalyticsConsent() === false` throughout.

**`mountAnalyticsConsentBanner` branch ordering (`AnalyticsConsentBanner.ts:55–57`).**
`hasPendingAnalyticsResetNotice()` checked first; if true, the reset notice mounts and returns. Only then does `hasSeenConsentPrompt()` run. Legacy users who had `prompt-seen = true` written by the old migration will have `hasPendingAnalyticsResetNotice() === true` (because `reason === 'legacy-reset'` and `RESET_NOTICE_SEEN_KEY !== 'true'`), so they see the reset notice rather than being silently dismissed.
